- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by adding 1–2% to forecast baseline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the 10–15 day horizon; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for high-sentiment periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.4 → -0.1 → +0.4), model fails to capture mean reversion; apply a “reversion penalty” to forecast: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-stage volatility; add 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive and price has not yet peaked in last 7 days.
